The graph shows a portion of the curve $y=\operatorname{sec}⁡x$ and the line $y=-2.$ Which of the following generates the $x$-values of all of their points of intersection? Assume that $n$ is an integer.
feedback.worked_solution:
At the intersection points, the $y$-values are the same for both graphs. This gives the equation $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=-2.$ 

Recall that $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x},$ therefore the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\text{arccos}(-\frac{1}{2})={120}^{∘}
$$

Our first solution lies in the $2$nd quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={60}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the $3$rd quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}={60}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13979076/assets/ec1135cb0a4d35130a1c11baf9f421a3cdb4bc22cc1b436686dce722fa3c812e.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$  lies in the $3$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}+{60}^{∘} \\  & ={240}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the general solution for the given equation is 

$$
x={120}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘},\,x={240}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.
$$
